column1: # Where each Old English interjection in lex-ang.tsv, and each target of more
# than one word, was read in a text.
# lemma | pos | tgt | sources | quotation
# A single word is checked against a dictionary entry wherever the pack makes
# a claim about it: its etymon in ang-etymons.tsv, its gender in
# ang-genders.tsv. A phrase had nothing, and a phrase is where this lexicon
# wrote Old English of its own. Of the four interjections it taught for a
# speech act, two were not what Old English said. far wel, goodbye, is in English
# Wiktionary only as the reconstruction "*far wel!", and was withdrawn on
# 2026-10-05 for wes hāl. mē is lāþ, sorry, is well formed, and
# Bosworth–Toller has it as loathing, not regret — "Ðá wæs ic swíðe
# onscúniende and mé láð wæs" glosses Latin "multum detestatus sum", I
# greatly detested (bt:21202). It was withdrawn the same day for mē hrēoweþ,
# "it rues me", the impersonal hrēowan, which the dictionary glosses "to rue,
# make sorry, grieve; often impers." and quotes with mē in Genesis.
# And one adverb. tōmorgen, woven for "tomorrow" until 2026-10-07, is one
# word in neither dictionary: Bosworth–Toller's morgen (bt:23129) prints
# "Tó morgen cras" from Exodus and the West Saxon Gospels, and "Gá and cum
# tó morgenne go, and come to-morrow" from the Pastoral Care. The pack
# writes tō morgen, the form all the other texts there have, and the card
# was renamed to it, its letters being the same.
# The quotation is the text the phrase was read in, as Bosworth–Toller prints
# it, with where it is from. tests/tools/phrases.test.ts requires each word
# of the phrase to stand in it, accents and macrons aside and ð read as þ, as
# a word or the start of one, so an inflected form counts: goodbye's line
# quotes the plural, "Wesaþ hále", because that is the form that glosses
# Latin "valete", farewell, where hello's is a greeting. It cannot tell a text
# somebody read from one somebody typed, the limit every ledger here has;
# but a phrase no text has cannot be given a quotation honestly, which is
# what the column is for.
# The sources field
# Each line names the entries the quotation was read in, separated by
# spaces, and at least one is Bosworth–Toller's:
#   bt:<id>            https://bosworthtoller.com/<id>
#   wikt:ang:<title>   https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/<title>#Old_English
# A line is never the only check on its phrase: its etymon, if it has one,
# is held by ang-etymons.tsv, and its card by card-ids.tsv. A phrase that
# leaves the pack keeps its card through WITHDRAWN in src/core/renames.ts.
